newsitem.title: POLAND: Early Polish zloty holds flat, market nervous.
newsitem.headline: Early Polish zloty holds flat, market nervous.

text.p: The Polish zloty narrowed in on one percent from parity in early Monday trade and local dealers were mixed on the local currency's near-term moves.

Some said that further foreign withdrawal from Polish treasuries could weaken the zloty, while others said capital inflows, such as funds for the public offer of copper concern KGHM Polska Miedz would keep the zloty under upward pressure.

"The zloty is straddling one percent from parity and it could remain at present levels for now...but several orders could create turbulence on the nervous market," said Piotr Czyzewski, foreign exchange dealer at ING Bank in Warsaw.
At 0820 GMT the zloty was at 1.03/1.00 percent from the parity rate, flat from opening's 1.05/0.97 percent.
It was at 3.2710/20 to the dollar, up from 3.2720/60 at 0700 GMT and at 1.8823/30 to the mark, down from 1.8807/12, in line with the U.S. unit's moves on world markets.

Some foreigners withdrew from Polish paper at the end of last week after the National Bank of Poland and the IMF warned that Poland may be headed for a Czech-style current account crisis if it failed to balance its budget quickly.
The goverment said a tight monetary policy and the planned 1998 budget gap reduction would keep the C/A deficit in check.

On the money market one-day rates remained high as the market tightened up on the first day of the July required reserve as banks entered the period with low average reserve levels and wanted to quickly rebuild positions, dealers said.
At 0830 GMT overnight rates were at 23.65/24.65 percent and tomorrow/next rates at 23.10/24.30 percent after opening at 24.15/24.60 and 23.45/24.65 percent respectively.
